title: 2022 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: Kayla rolls four fair \(6\)-sided dice. What is the probability that at least one of the numbers Kayla rolls is greater than \(4\) and at least two of the numbers she rolls are greater than \(2?\)

solutions.text:
Sort each die into low \(\{1,2\},\) mid \(\{3,4\},\) or high \(\{5,6\};\) each has probability \(\tfrac13,\) so the \(3^4 = 81\) category patterns are equally likely.

We need at least one high die (a number greater than \(4\)) and at least two dice that are greater than \(2\) (mid or high). The two bad events are having no high die and having at most one non-low die.

There are \(2^4 = 16\) patterns of the first kind, \(9\) of the second kind, and \(5\) in their intersection. By inclusion-exclusion the count of good patterns is \(81 - 16 - 9 + 5 = 61.\)

The probability is \(\dfrac{61}{81}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Sort each die into low \(\{1,2\},\) mid \(\{3,4\},\) or high \(\{5,6\},\) each with probability \(\tfrac13\)
You need at least one high die and at least two dice that are not low; count the good category patterns out of \(3^4\)
